The king moves one square in any direction. In a match it cannot move into check.
The queen moves along ranks, files and diagonals. It cannot jump over pieces.
The rook moves along ranks and files. It cannot jump over pieces.
The bishop moves diagonally and stays on the same square colour. It cannot jump over pieces.
The knight moves two squares one way and one sideways, making an L. It can jump over pieces.
A White pawn moves one square forward, or two from its starting rank if clear. It captures one square diagonally forward and cannot move backwards.

Example: select the piece, then tap the target square.
If you are new to chess
Try Meet the Pieces and Set Up the Board first. Find the rules and history of chess in General Information.
Practise in Practise, Protect Your King, Checkmate and Stalemate, and Mate in One.
Discover the first moves with Learn openings. Play the Computer or prepare a special position in Create Your Game.
Read about the rules, the aim of the game and the history of chess.
You can play explanations that have a Listen button.
Look at pictures of chess masters and read their short biographies.
Tap the card for a chess piece you are curious about.
2D and 3D change how the chess pieces look; the movement rules stay the same.
On the chess piece's page, listen to its name, look at the movement example and open practice.
How does this chess piece move?
Listen to its name and explanation
Use the buttons with a sound-wave icon.
Look at the demonstrated chess moves together with the explanation.
This button opens practice so you can try moving the chess piece yourself.
Read or listen to the instruction
The screen tells you which chess piece to put on which square.
Choose the chess piece and tap the right square, or drag it onto that square.
Black chess pieces appear automatically after you finish the white ones. Restart resets the setup.
In free practice, choose a chess piece; in task mode, follow the on-screen instruction.
Tap a square the chess piece can move to, or drag where placement is supported. Follow the feedback.
Tasks appear randomly. Finish a round, then practise again with new tasks.
Look at the attack on the chessboard, then read or listen to the instruction.
Tap the chess piece you want to move, then its destination square. Do not leave your king in check.
After the right chess move, go to the next task. A new round brings different tasks.
Is the king in check? Is there any legal move to escape?
Checkmate: the king is in check with no legal escape. Stalemate: the king is not in check, but there is no legal move. Check: the king is threatened, but a legal escape exists.
When the escape list appears, tap a move to see where the piece goes. Complete ten tasks.
Think about which chess move would stop every escape.
Choose the chess piece, then tap its destination. The aim is checkmate in one move.
Read the feedback. After the right answer, continue to the next task; a round has ten tasks.
The turn indicator is above the chessboard. On your turn, tap your chess piece, then its destination square.
Hint suggests a chess move. Undo takes back your last turn. In move history, you can inspect the chess pieces and squares.
Use the narration option on the board and choose the clock on the new game screen. If the clock is on, move before your time runs out.
The game saves automatically. A warning appears before a new game starts. The clock and computer moves wait while this help is open.
Choose white or black, select a chess piece and tap a square. You can also drag chess pieces into place.
Automatic arrangement places the starting army. Random arrangement places 1–16 chess pieces of the selected color, including one king, and keeps the opponent's pieces.
Eraser removes a chess piece, Undo reverses your last edit, and Clear board removes all chess pieces.
Choose your color, the side to move first and the difficulty. Each side needs one king. If the position is not ready, follow the explanation below; otherwise tap Start game.
Tap cards about opening principles, such as controlling the center and developing your chess pieces.
Open the Italian Game, Spanish Opening or another opening you are curious about.
Listen at the bottom of the page plays the explanations.
Learn an opening step by step
In watch mode, advance through the chess moves in order. Notice where each chess piece moves and the idea behind the move.
In practice mode, make the next chess move shown in the sequence. Hint helps you find the expected move.
Use back or restart to practise again. Listen is at the bottom. Other legal opening moves are possible besides this example.
Choose to play with white or black chess pieces.
Pick the level card that suits you.
New game asks for confirmation. If you confirm, the current game's move history is deleted. In a custom game, your prepared starting position is reused.

Tap Continue to go to the next word. Use Previous to go back.
Practise what you have learned with Listen and Choose, Match Pairs or Memory Cards.

Tap the picture that matches the word. If it is wrong, you can try another picture.

Matching cards stay face up. Two cards that do not match close after about one second. Find every pair!
See your progress in learning new words, reviewing words and completing games here.

Complete all three tasks to earn the daily reward. Goals reset each day.

Choose one of the supported languages for the app menus.
Choose the language you want to study. If needed, download its pack from Language packs.
Choose the pack for the language you want to study from the list.
Install the pack with its download or install button. Wait for it to finish; downloading may need an internet connection.
When the pack is ready, choose your learning language and open lessons and games.
Your child's name, selected companion, profile photo, learning progress and preferences are stored on this device.

Only the photo you select from the gallery is read. You can also choose to use the camera. A small copy is stored in the app's private storage on this device; your original gallery photo is not changed.
Installed language packs work offline. An internet connection is used to download or update the package catalog and the packs you select. Removing a language pack does not delete learning progress.

Achievement cards are prepared only when you open sharing. Use Share in the preview to send the card to the Android share menu and choose an app. Your child's name and profile photo are not included in the cards. Prepared cards are stored in the app's temporary cache.
Firebase crash reporting, push notifications and usage analytics are not enabled in this Android version.
To delete local data, clear the app's storage in Android settings or uninstall the app. This removes the profile photo, downloaded packs and learning progress stored on this device.
